# GoldenFlow Action

> Standardize, clean and normalize data files in CI, report the transforms applied, and post a pull-request comment.

## Usage

```yaml
- uses: benseverndev-oss/goldenmatch/packages/actions/goldenflow@main
  with:
    files: "data/*.csv"
```

## Inputs

- `files` -- glob for the data files to transform (required)
- `config` -- path to a goldenflow YAML config
- `domain` -- domain pack to apply, e.g. `people_hr`, `healthcare`
- `strict` -- fail the job if any transform errored (default false)
- `python-version` -- Python to run on
- `version` -- goldenflow version to install

## Outputs

- `transforms-applied`, `files-processed`, `errors`

## Authoritative sources

Read these instead of inferring behaviour from `action.yml`. An input list
gives you names and types; it cannot tell you which defaults are deliberate
or what a knob protects against:

- https://docs.bensevern.dev/docs/goldenflow -- full documentation for the underlying tool.
- `goldenflow/llms.txt` -- ships inside the goldenflow wheel this action installs (`Path(goldenflow.__file__).parent / "llms.txt"`), written for machine readers.
- https://docs.bensevern.dev/docs/llms.txt -- index of every Golden Suite surface.
- https://github.com/benseverndev-oss/goldenmatch -- source, issues, and the decision records.

## Things that are decided, not incidental

- **The job passes by default even when transforms error.** GoldenFlow lets a value it cannot parse pass through unchanged rather than failing, and the action follows suit -- errors land in the `errors` output and the PR comment, but do not fail the check. Set `strict: true` when you would rather the build break than let an unrecognised value through.
- The transform set is single-sourced from a Rust kernel shared with the Python, TypeScript and SQL surfaces, so the same input standardizes identically wherever it runs -- CI and production do not drift.
